steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the fs (file system) and path modules using require()
steps.hint: Use require('moduleName') to import Node.js core modules. Both modules are built-in, so no npm installation is needed.
steps.seedCode: // Import fs and path modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The fs and path modules are imported and ready to use for file operations and path handling.
successCriteria: fs and path are imported using require()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the fs and path modules. These will be essential for reading/writing files and handling file paths.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both fs and path modules using require().
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import both the fs and path modules using require().

steps.title: Create test data directory path constant
steps.instruction: Define a constant variable named TEST_DATA_DIR that points to a 'test-data' directory in your project using path.join() with __dirname.
steps.hint: Use path.join() to combine __dirname with the directory name 'test-data'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a directory path constant
const DATA_DIR = path.join(__dirname, 'data');
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a constant TEST_DATA_DIR that stores the absolute path to a test-data directory.
successCriteria: The constant TEST_DATA_DIR is defined using path.join() with __dirname and 'test-data'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the test data directory path constant.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using path.join() with __dirname and the directory name 'test-data'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Try defining a constant TEST_DATA_DIR using path.join(__dirname, 'test-data').

steps.title: Create test data factory function skeleton
steps.instruction: Define a function called createTestData that takes filename and data as parameters. The function body can be empty for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. The function should accept two parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createTestData is defined with filename and data parameters.
successCriteria: The createTestData function is defined with two parameters: filename and data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the skeleton for the test data factory function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named createTestData and accepts both filename and data parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's named createTestData and accepts two parameters.

steps.title: Implement file creation logic in factory
steps.instruction: Inside the createTestData function, use fs.writeFileSync to write the provided data to a file in the test directory. Use the path.join method to create the full file path.
steps.hint: Remember that writeFileSync takes the file path and data as arguments. You'll need to combine the test directory path with a filename.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createTestData function will be able to write test data to a file when called.
successCriteria: The createTestData function contains fs.writeFileSync with proper file path construction using path.join.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented the file creation logic using fs.writeFileSync.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using fs.writeFileSync and constructing the file path with path.join.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file creation logic isn't implemented correctly. Review how to use fs.writeFileSync and path.join.

steps.title: Add error handling to factory function
steps.instruction: Wrap the file writing logic inside the createTestData function with a try-catch block to handle potential errors.
steps.hint: Use try { ... } catch (error) { ... } around the fs.writeFileSync call.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createTestData function will have a try-catch block that wraps the file writing logic.
successCriteria: The createTestData function contains a try-catch block that encloses the fs.writeFileSync call.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added error handling to the factory function, making it more robust.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started adding error handling, but make sure the try-catch block properly wraps the file writing logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: The try-catch block is missing or incorrectly placed. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Create cleanup utility function skeleton
steps.instruction: Define a function called cleanupTestData that takes a filename as a parameter. The function body can be empty for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Remember to include the filename parameter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: a function with a parameter
function deleteFile(filename) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: A cleanupTestData function skeleton is added to the file, ready for implementation in later steps.
successCriteria: The cleanupTestData function is defined with a filename parameter and an empty body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the cleanup utility function skeleton. This will be used to remove test files after testing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named cleanupTestData that accepts a filename parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanupTestData function isn't properly defined. Check that you've used the correct function name and parameter.

steps.title: Implement file deletion logic in cleanup
steps.instruction: Inside the cleanupTestData function, use fs.unlinkSync to delete the specified test file. The function should take a filename parameter and delete that file from the TEST_DATA_DIR.
steps.hint: Use path.join to create the full file path, then call fs.unlinkSync with that path. Don't forget to handle errors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanupTestData function should be able to delete a specified file from the test-data directory using synchronous file operations.
successCriteria: cleanupTestData function uses fs.unlinkSync to delete files and includes proper path construction with path.join
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the file deletion logic in the cleanup utility.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using fs.unlinkSync and constructing the full file path with path.join.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanupTestData function doesn't properly implement file deletion. Review how to use fs.unlinkSync and path.join.

steps.title: Add error handling to cleanup function
steps.instruction: Wrap the file deletion logic in your cleanupTestData function with a try-catch block to handle cases where files don't exist during cleanup.
steps.hint: Use try { ... } catch (error) { ... } around the fs.unlinkSync call, and consider returning a status object or boolean to indicate success/failure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanupTestData function should now include error handling that catches deletion errors (e.g., when the file doesn't exist) and returns a status indicating what happened.
successCriteria: The cleanupTestData function contains a try-catch block around the file deletion logic and returns a status object or boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added proper error handling to the cleanup function, making it robust for cases where files might not exist.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to wrap the deletion logic in try-catch and return a status from the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function still lacks error handling. Add a try-catch block to handle file deletion errors.

steps.title: Create sample test data object
steps.instruction: Define a sample data object with properties like id, name, and value. Add this object after your cleanupTestData function.
steps.hint: Create a simple JavaScript object with key-value pairs that represent typical test data.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sample test data object is created with properties like id, name, and value.
successCriteria: A sample data object is defined with at least id, name, and value properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a sample test data object with the required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created an object, but make sure it includes properties like id, name, and value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample test data object is missing or doesn't have the expected structure.

steps.title: Test the data factory with sample data
steps.instruction: Call the createTestData function with a test filename and the sample data object you created earlier.
steps.hint: Use the function name createTestData and pass two arguments: a string for the filename and your sample data object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of calling a function with arguments
createTestData('sample.json', { name: 'Test', value: 123 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The createTestData function will be called with actual arguments, allowing you to test its functionality.
successCriteria: createTestData is called with a filename string and the sample data object as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the data factory function with test data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createTestData with both a filename and your sample data object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function call is missing or incorrect. You need to call createTestData with two arguments.

steps.title: Test the cleanup utility
steps.instruction: Call the cleanupTestData function with the same test filename you used in the previous step.
steps.hint: You need to invoke cleanupTestData and pass the filename string that matches the file created by createTestData.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: calling a function with a filename
cleanupTestData('test-file.txt');
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanup function will be executed to remove the test file, verifying the cleanup utility works.
successCriteria: cleanupTestData is called with a valid filename string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested the cleanup utility by calling it with the test filename.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling cleanupTestData with the exact filename string used in the previous step.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function wasn't called correctly. Check that you're invoking cleanupTestData with a filename argument.

steps.title: Export the utility functions
steps.instruction: Export both the createTestData and cleanupTestData functions using module.exports so they can be imported in other modules.
steps.hint: Add a module.exports statement at the end of your file, assigning an object with both function names as properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both functions are properly exported and ready for use in other Node.js modules.
successCriteria: The createTestData and cleanupTestData functions are exported using module.exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported both utility functions. They can now be imported and used in other test files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're exporting both functions (createTestData and cleanupTestData) in the module.exports statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using module.exports to export both functions. The export should be at the end of the file.
